the expression of proinsulin and its derivatives is not significantly affected by the presence of additional sequences in the 5'-untranslated region or by multiple copies of the gene.

the expression, processing, refolding and purification, of human proinsulins, is not affected by the presence of a linker, the nature of the amino acids in the linker or by the presence of additional proinsulin genes, in the constructs, or of the presence of the proinsulins in the form of inclusion bodies.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proinsulin derivatives, which were expressed, were efficiently processed to give insulin derivatives.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of proinsulin derivatives, with a trypsin cleavage site before the C-terminal F residue, is not a prerequisite for efficient conversion into insulin derivatives.
the proinsulin genes can be expressed efficiently and the products can be processed efficiently to give insulin derivatives.

the expression of proteins in E. coli is largely independent of the sequence surrounding the start of translation, and that the expression of proinsulin and derivatives is best achieved by the use of a synthetic gene with an N-terminal methionyl residue.
